nh_pawtuckaway.blurb: Pawtuckaway, in the town of Nottingham in southern New Hampshire, is mainly a bouldering destination. Glacial erratic boulders are scattered through the forest, with smaller cliffs among them, and the rock is granite. Bouldering makes up the vast majority of the climbing, with a broad spread from easy problems into the hard V grades, plus cracks, arêtes, slopers and highballs. Boulder Natural and Blair Woods hold the most problems. Trad and top-rope climbing is on short cliffs such as Devil's Den, Upper Cliff and the Lower Slabs, mostly moderate to 5.11 with a few harder lines, and only a handful of bolted routes exist. Autumn is the pleasant season; spring and early summer bring heavy biting insects.

nm_albuquerque_area.blurb: Climbing around Albuquerque centers on the Sandia Mountains, which rise directly east of the city. The range has a granite core, and its steep west side holds towers, ridges and walls for traditional and multi-pitch climbing; the rock quality is variable and many approaches are long. Trad is the largest share here, followed by bouldering and then sport, mostly from 5.8 to 5.12, with plenty of moderates. Foothills Bouldering is the second biggest sub-area and suits warm winter days. Palomas Peak, on the east side, offers bolted limestone sport climbing that is best in spring and fall. Cliffs up near the crest stay cooler in summer, though afternoon thunderstorms are common on the west face.

ut_west_desert.blurb: The West Desert is the wide, remote basin-and-range country of western Utah, with climbing scattered across many separate mountain ranges and a great variety of rock. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, mainly 5.9 to 5.12, alongside trad lines and a good amount of bouldering. Ibex has textured quartzite beside a dry salt flat and is known for its bouldering, with some routes too. The House Range mixes granite crags with large limestone walls, the Stansbury Mountains hold hard limestone sport climbing, and the Oquirrh Mountains and Devil's Playground and Spires add more. Spring and fall suit most areas, while the higher Stansbury and Oquirrh crags can be comfortable in summer. Expect an adventurous feel, long drives and almost no phone signal.

ca_owens_river_gorge.blurb: Owens River Gorge is a steep canyon, about ten miles long, on the eastern edge of the Sierra Nevada in southern Mono County, north of Bishop. The river has cut through a thick layer of welded volcanic tuff, which gives edges, pockets and cracks on mostly vertical walls, with a few steeper lines. It is a modern sport area: nearly everything is bolted, with a small share of trad. Grades cluster at 5.10 to 5.12, with a decent number of moderates below 5.10 and a few harder lines. The gorge is split into Upper, Central, Inner, Lower, Sub and North sections, with Central the largest. It climbs year-round, though summer can be hot, and the popular spots are often crowded.

va_guest_river_gorge.blurb: Guest River Gorge lies beside the Guest River near Coeburn in far southwest Virginia. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing here, with problems across a wide range from easy into the harder V grades and a thick middle of moderates, while sport routes account for roughly a quarter and run from 5.8 up to the low 5.13s, with the heaviest concentration around 5.10 to 5.12. A small amount of trad is also found. The gorge is organized by distance along the river, as Mile One through Mile Five, with Mile Two and Mile One holding the most routes. Jaybird Gorge is the single biggest sub-area.

sd_spearfish_canyon.blurb: Spearfish Canyon is South Dakota's main sport-climbing canyon, with walls of pocketed limestone known for overhanging, physical lines. Bolted routes dominate by a wide margin, and the grades concentrate at 5.10 to 5.13, with the heart of it around 5.11 and 5.12. Easier options exist but are limited, and Sunshine, the largest sub-area, is the usual place for newer leaders. Other big sectors include The Mohican, Shadowlands, Blue Sky and Big Picture Gully, and there is a modest amount of bouldering too. The canyon climbs nearly year-round: Sunshine is warm in winter and its walls shade in summer afternoons, and frozen waterfalls draw ice climbers in midwinter.
